title: World Foundation raises $52 million in token sale as proof-of-human demand accelerates

content_html:
TL;DR

World Foundation raised $52M via locked token sale led by Pantera Capital to expand World ID proof-of-human tech across enterprise platforms

World Foundation has raised $52 million through a locked token sale to expand the reach of World ID, its iris-scan-based system for proving someone is a real human online. Pantera Capital led the initial close, joined by Bain Capital Crypto, Eightco Holdings, Selini Capital, and Susquehanna Crypto, with all WLD tokens sold subject to a 12-month lockup. The fundraise lands on the third anniversary of the project’s launch and follows a $135 million token sale led by Andreessen Horowitz and Bain Capital Crypto in May 2025.

The capital will fund World ID’s expansion into enterprise platforms that are already integrating the technology. Zoom began using World’s Deep Face verification in April to prove meeting participants are human, displaying a “Verified Human” badge when a live video feed matches a user’s iris-scanned biometric profile. Docusign, Okta, Vercel, and Tinder have also signed integration deals, each addressing a different vector of the same problem: bots and deepfakes eroding trust on digital platforms.

World ID works by having users visit a physical Orb device that scans their iris and generates a unique cryptographic credential stored on their phone. The system uses zero-knowledge proofs and what World calls anonymised multi-party computation to verify someone is a unique human without revealing their identity. More than 39 million people have joined the World Network to date, with more than 18 million verified through an Orb across 160 countries.

The project, originally conceived by Sam Altman, Max Novendstern, and Alex Blania, has faced sustained regulatory pushback over its biometric data collection. Spain ordered the company to halt iris scanning in 2024 over privacy concerns, and Germany’s data regulator mandated the deletion of iris data later that year. Kenya, Hong Kong, Argentina, and the Philippines have all taken enforcement action against the project, citing issues ranging from insufficient consent to the use of cryptocurrency incentives to recruit participants in lower-income communities.

World Foundation says the new funding will also support World ID version four, an enterprise-ready upgrade that lets third-party developers build their own credentials into the system’s zero-knowledge proof stack. The timing reflects a bet that the same AI systems making bots indistinguishable from humans will force platforms to adopt proof-of-human infrastructure, though the gap between enterprise demand for verified identity and the regulatory resistance to how World collects that identity remains the central tension the project has yet to resolve.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

World Foundation 通过由 Pantera Capital 牵头的锁定代币销售筹集了 5200 万美元，以在企业平台上扩展 World ID 人类技术证明

World Foundation 通过锁定代币销售筹集了 5200 万美元，以扩大 World ID 的覆盖范围，World ID 是其基于虹膜扫描的系统，用于证明某人是在线真人。 Pantera Capital 领投，Bain Capital Crypto、Eightco Holdings、Selini Capital 和 Susquehanna Crypto 跟投，所有出售的 WLD 代币都有 12 个月的锁定期。 此次融资是在该项目启动三周年之际进行的，此前，Andreessen Horowitz 和 Bain Capital Crypto 于 2025 年 5 月主导了 1.35 亿美元的代币销售。

该资金将资助 World ID 扩展到已经集成该技术的企业平台。 Zoom 从四月份开始使用 World 的 Deep Face 验证来证明会议参与者是人类，当实时视频源与用户的虹膜扫描生物识别资料匹配时，会显示“经过验证的人类”徽章。 Docusign、Okta、Vercel 和 Tinder 也签署了整合协议，各自解决同一问题的不同方面：机器人和 Deepfakes 侵蚀数字平台的信任。

World ID 的工作原理是让用户访问物理 Orb 设备，该设备扫描他们的虹膜并生成存储在手机上的唯一加密凭证。 该系统使用零知识证明和 World 所谓的匿名多方计算来验证某人是否是唯一的人，而无需透露其身份。 迄今为止，已有超过 3900 万人加入了世界网络，其中超过 1800 万人通过 160 个国家/地区的 Orb 进行了验证。

该项目最初由 Sam Altman、Max Novendstern 和 Alex Blania 构想，但因其生物识别数据收集而面临持续的监管阻力。 出于隐私考虑，西班牙下令该公司在 2024 年停止虹膜扫描，德国数据监管机构于当年晚些时候下令删除虹膜数据。 肯尼亚、香港、阿根廷和菲律宾都对该项目采取了执法行动，理由包括未充分同意以及使用加密货币激励措施来招募低收入社区的参与者等问题。

世界基金会表示，新资金还将支持 World ID 第四版，这是一项企业级升级，可让第三方开发人员将自己的凭证构建到系统的零知识证明堆栈中。 这一时机反映了一种押注，即使机器人与人类无法区分的相同人工智能系统将迫使平台采用人类证明基础设施，尽管企业对经过验证的身份的需求与 World 收集身份的监管阻力之间的差距仍然是该项目尚未解决的主要紧张局势。
